I am 70 years old and I have farmed in Quzhou County my whole life. My family has 8 mu of flat land on the North China Plain. The winter wheat I sowed last October is starting to green up now, so this year's plan is the same as always: bring the wheat through to harvest in early June, then immediately plant summer maize. I would never gamble on cotton or vegetables — the wheat-maize double crop is the only system I trust to feed my family and produce a stable income. I am getting older and my back isn't what it used to be, so my son operates the tractor and helps carry fertilizer bags. I buy improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed from the supply store in town because they give higher yields than saving my own seed. For fertilizer, the extension leaflet says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu for wheat, but I always apply 16 kg — I learned long ago that being slightly generous is safer than risking a yield drop. I apply compound fertilizer as base and urea as topdressing. I will irrigate the wheat four times: at green-up, jointing, heading, and grain filling. The maize will get two irrigations, one at sowing and one at filling. For tillage, I rotary-tilled before planting the wheat last autumn, but for maize there is no time to plough after wheat harvest — I plant no-tillage, which also saves labor. I spray pesticides three times on wheat and twice on maize, mainly for weeds and corn borer. I expect about 500 kg per mu for wheat and 550 kg per mu for maize, which matches what I have gotten in recent years.
